# REGIME READ — 2026-09-14

**[FULL READ — WebSearch was available this run, for the first time in four sessions.]** Every carried-forward figure from the 2026-09-08 read has been refreshed or replaced. Two things changed materially as a result, and both are bad. One prior finding is withdrawn as a misdiagnosis.

## Changes Since Previous Read
- **Stage: 3 (Neutral/choppy) → 3 (Neutral/choppy)** — unchanged for a thirteenth consecutive read. VIX **17.50** sits inside the 15–22 band. **But the composition of that classification changed in an important way: for the first time, the "breadth deteriorating" half of the Stage-4 definition is unambiguously satisfied, and only the VIX level is holding Stage 3.** See the Stage Tracker.
- **Total score: −7 → −9 (delta −2).** **A new series low, ending a four-read plateau at −7.** **Two lenses flipped — the first lens movement in five reads.**
- **Triggers from previous read:**
  - *Bearish — CPI at or above +0.4% m/m:* **FIRED.** **August headline CPI rose +0.4% m/m, 12-month rate 3.4%** (BLS/CNBC, 2026-09-11). Core +0.3% m/m (0.29%), **0.1pp above forecast**, core y/y 2.4%. **Gasoline rose 3.9% m/m and 27.4% y/y, accounting for over one third of the entire monthly increase.** **CME FedWatch odds of a 25bp September hike moved to 85%** (2026-09-14), from ~52–66% when last measurable. **This is the regime trigger, not a mechanical one, and I am honouring it — the put-selling context moves to HOSTILE.**
  - *Bullish — CPI ≤ +0.2% m/m pulling hike odds below ~35%:* **REFUTED outright.** Print was double that; odds went the other way, to 85%.
  - *Bearish — TQQQ closes below the 4-week low $67.93:* **CLEARED on the close and re-armed in premarket.** TQQQ **closed $70.98 on 2026-09-11, +2.56%**, now **4.30% above** the 4-week low. **But QQQ is −1.45% in Monday premarket (TheStreet, 2026-09-14), which at 3× maps to roughly −4.35% on TQQQ, or about $67.89 — essentially at the 4-week low.** Premarket, not a close.
  - *Bullish — TQQQ reclaims the 50DMA and holds:* **ARMED, and it missed by a dime.** Spot **$70.98** against a 50DMA that fell to **$71.05** — **−0.10%**, the closest of the series. Not reclaimed.
  - *Bearish — Brent back above $105 and holding two sessions:* **ARMED, one leg only.** Brent **closed $104.61 on 09-11 (−2.81%)** — below the line — then **jumped to $108.48 (+3.70%) in Monday trade, a near-4-month high.** Needs a second consecutive close above $105.
  - *Bullish — Brent back below $92:* **ARMED and moved sharply away.** Needs **−15.19%** (was −10.8%).
  - *Bearish — VXN > 25:* **ARMED and moved sharply away.** **VXN crushed −9.90% to 21.02** on the print. Needs **+18.93%**, from +7.2%. **The fastest-closing trigger in the last four reports reversed in a single session.**
  - *Bullish — NDX ≥ 30,000 with VXN < 19:* **ARMED, both legs narrowed for the first time in four sessions.** NDX **29,368.44** needs **+2.15%** (was 3.08%); VXN **21.02** needs **−9.61%** (was 4.33 above 19, now 2.02 above).
  - *Bearish — NDX < 28,400:* **ARMED, further away.** Needs **−3.30%** (was −2.42%).
  - *Bearish — HY OAS through 3.25% WITH IG above 0.90%:* **ARMED, both legs improved by 1bp — and both readings PREDATE the print.** HY **2.70%**, IG **0.80%**, both stamped **2026-09-10** (FRED). **Credit has not been observable since CPI. This is now the largest measurement gap in the report.**
  - *Bearish — VIX/VIX3M term ratio ≥ 1.00:* **UNMEASURABLE this run** — the chain fetch returned n/a for every option-derived field. Last read 0.904.
  - *Bullish — confirmed US–China tariff reduction:* **PARTIALLY CONFIRMED, and my previous read was right to flag it.** **A Trump–Xi summit is set for Washington on 2026-09-24**, with both sides working toward **reciprocal tariff reductions on $30 billion of goods each** "at an early date" (Business Day/CNBC, 2026-09-10). **Real, verified, and ten days out — but no agreement yet.**
  - *Neutralizer — CPI 2026-09-11:* **RESOLVED. Hot on the headline, in line on the 12-month rate, 0.1pp hot on core, and the market rallied anyway on falling oil. See Diverging Signals.**
- **Notable lens flips — two, the first movement in five reads.** **Lens 4 Breadth −1 → −2** on refreshed data that is far worse than the figures I had been carrying. **Lens 5 Cross-asset −1 → −2** on a physical oil supply outage. **Lens count: 0 bullish, 5 bearish, 2 neutral — fifth consecutive read with no bullish lens.**

**Friday 2026-09-11 broke the losing streak and every index closed higher.** **DJI +0.98% led, then NDX +0.91%, Nasdaq Composite +0.96%, SPX +0.86%, Russell 2000 +0.45% last.** The driver was not the inflation print itself — **stocks rose because oil fell 2.81% that day, outweighing sticky inflation** (Yahoo Finance midday report, 2026-09-11). **VIX plunged 11.21% to close at 15.84.** **Despite the Friday bounce, the week was negative across the board: SPX −0.8%, Nasdaq −0.7%, Dow −1.6%, Russell 2000 −2.4%** (CNBC weekly wrap).

**And the reason Friday's relief does not carry is sitting in the 09-14 rows.** **Brent has reversed the entire Friday fall and more, to $108.48 (+3.70%), a near-four-month high**, after **Saudi Arabia shut its East-West crude pipeline** — the route used to bypass the Strait of Hormuz — and after the **Iran–Gulf talks in Muscat on a temporary Hormuz shipping corridor were postponed** (CBS News, Bloomberg, 2026-09-14). **VIX has re-spiked 10.48% off Friday's 15.84 close to 17.50.** **QQQ is −1.45% in premarket on an AI and semiconductor selloff** (TheStreet, 2026-09-14). **In plain terms: the one thing that made Friday feel good has been undone over a weekend, and the market is opening Monday lower with a near-certain rate hike two days out.**

**Day-change reconciliation — and a correction to four consecutive reads.** All seven settled rows reconcile exactly against the prior read: **SPX +0.86%, NDX +0.91%, Nasdaq Composite +0.96%, DJI +0.98%, Russell +0.45%, 10Y +0.63%, VXN −9.90%** — every one to the basis point. **The four later-stamped rows also reconcile, and this is where I have to correct myself.** Backing out each row's implied basis: **VIX 17.50 at +10.48% implies a prior close of 15.84 — which web-verification confirms is exactly Friday's VIX close.** **Brent 108.48 at +3.70% implies 104.61 — exactly Friday's Brent close.** **The column is correct. It compares each row to that row's own prior CLOSE.** The error was mine: for four reads I compared today's **pre-open quote** to yesterday's report's **pre-open quote**, called the difference the day change, and escalated the resulting mismatch to an "urgent" data defect. **Finding 3 is withdrawn — see the footnote.**

## Regime Stage Tracker
- **Current Stage:** **3 — Neutral / choppy**, and the reason has narrowed to one number. VIX **17.50** sits inside the 15–22 band; VXN **21.02** likewise. **No Stage-4 threshold has fired: VIX needs +14.29% to reach 20, VXN needs +18.93% to reach 25, NDX needs −3.30%, HY OAS needs +55bp.** **But Stage 4 is defined as "VIX 20–30 rising AND breadth deteriorating", and the breadth half is now unambiguously true: 33% of S&P 500 members are above their 50-day average, down from 63.6%; 331 new yearly lows on the NYSE, the most since the March/April 2026 correction; the NYSE advance-decline line has broken prior support** (StockCharts, 2026-09-11). **For twelve reads I wrote that credit was the load-bearing member holding this classification. That is no longer true. The load-bearing member is the VIX level, and nothing else. A move to 20 flips the stage with no further confirmation required from anywhere.**
- **Stage Anchor:** **2026-08-28 — Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote**, which pushed market-implied September hike odds from roughly even to a majority (CNBC/Forbes 2026-08-28/31). **The anchor has now largely played out: odds are 85% and the decision is Wednesday.** The **US–Iran conflict** (from 2026-02-28) amplifies via the oil channel and re-escalated this weekend.
- **Position:** Week 3 of the rate-repricing leg, inside a Stage-3 range confirmed across thirteen consecutive reads (08-28 through 09-14). **The event the leg was building toward lands on session 3 of this week.**
- **Confidence:** **High.** Five lenses bearish (Macro −2, Breadth −2, Cross-asset −2, Geopolitical −2, Dealer flow −1), none bullish, two neutral — five aligned meets the High threshold. **Unlike the previous three reads there is no degradation cap: WebSearch was available and the macro, breadth, sentiment and geopolitical inputs were all verified today.**
- **Bullish trigger (→ Stage 2):** NDX ≥ **30,000** (+2.15%) **with** VXN below **19** (−9.61%); **or** Brent back below **$92** (−15.19%) on a Hormuz de-escalation; **or** a dovish FOMC surprise on Wednesday — no hike, or a hike paired with a dot plot showing no further moves.
- **Bearish trigger (→ Stage 4):** VIX sustained above **20** (+14.29% — **now the single hinge of the stage classification**); **or** **VXN > 25** (+18.93%); **or** NDX < **28,400** (−3.30%); **or** **HY OAS through 3.25% with IG above 0.90%** (from 2.70% / 0.80%, both pre-CPI).

## Regime Verdict
A Stage-3 range now held together by the VIX level alone — breadth has collapsed to correction-grade internals behind indices near their highs, oil has broken to a four-month high on a physical pipeline outage, the inflation print fired the hostile trigger and pushed hike odds to 85% two days before the decision, and no lens in this report is positive — at **High** confidence.

**Data note — this is a FULL read.** WebSearch was available and everything carried since 2026-09-08 has been refreshed: CPI actuals, FedWatch odds, breadth, Fear & Greed, the Hormuz situation, the US–China summit. **What I could NOT obtain this run is different from previous runs and it is option-market data: the chain fetch returned n/a for TQQQ ATM IV, put/call, the VIX/VIX3M term ratio, live spot and IV/HV.** Layer 2's volatility section therefore falls back to the 3×VXN heuristic, which this series has measured running 13–15% hot against the real quote. **Also unrefreshed: HY and IG OAS carry 2026-09-10 FRED stamps and so predate the CPI print entirely** — credit has not been observable across the event that matters. **Never retrieved in any read:** AAII, CFTC COT, margin debt, ETF flows, Citi Economic Surprise, insider/buyback activity, Copper/Gold, BTC, transports. **NAAIM remains paywalled since 2026-08-01.**

## Diverging Signals

**First, and it is the finding of this read: the indices and their internals have been telling different stories for a week, and I could not see it because my breadth numbers were five sessions old.** **Refreshed: 33% of S&P 500 members above their 50-day average (from 63.6%), 53% above their 200-day (from 67.1%), 331 new NYSE yearly lows — the most since a correction that took the S&P down over 20% — the advance-decline line through prior support, and the McClellan Oscillator oversold. All of that with SPX roughly 2–3% from all-time highs.** **For five reads I wrote that three consecutive all-red sessions on healthy internals was a tension I could not resolve and that breadth was my least-evidenced score. The resolution is simply that the internals were not healthy.** **A third of the index holding up the whole index is the single most important number in this report, and it was invisible for as long as WebSearch was.**

**Second: the market rallied on a hot inflation print, and the reason it did has since been reversed.** **CPI came in at +0.4% m/m with core 0.1pp above forecast, and stocks rose — because Brent fell 2.81% that day, and falling oil outweighed sticky inflation** (Yahoo Finance, 2026-09-11). **VIX plunged 11.21% to 15.84.** **Over the weekend Saudi Arabia shut a pipeline and the Hormuz talks were postponed, Brent is +3.70% to $108.48, VIX is +10.48%, and QQQ is −1.45% in premarket.** **In plain terms: Friday's rally rested entirely on the one variable that has now moved the other way, and it rested on it while the inflation data itself was hot. That is a fragile foundation, and it has already given.**

**Third: at-the-money volatility collapsed while crash protection hit a record. Those are not the same market.** **VXN −9.90% to 21.02 and VIX to 15.84 on Friday say the event passed. SKEW at 154.49, a new series high, says the tail is the most expensive it has been all series.** **A put seller is compensated by the first number and exposed to the second.** **The plain reading: dealers are relaxed about the next 1%, and unusually unrelaxed about the next 10%. That combination is the least attractive one for selling downside — you are paid on the part that got cheap and you carry the part that got expensive.**

**Fourth: the trigger that fired was the regime trigger, and the label moves. That is what the re-specification was for.** **Last read I published CAUTIOUS while my own $70.00 threshold had fired, recorded it as Finding 6 against myself, and re-specified all five thresholds to state a regime condition alongside a level.** **The re-specification was immediately tested in both directions and passed both.** **In the lenient direction: TQQQ closed back above $70 two sessions later, at $70.98 — the mechanical break I declined to treat as a regime change was indeed not one.** **In the strict direction: CPI printed +0.4% m/m, which is a stated regime condition and not a price artefact, and I am honouring it without argument.** **The put-selling context is HOSTILE for the first time in this series.**

**Fifth: the news daemon failed in the opposite direction from last read, which means it is uncalibrated rather than merely over-sensitive.** **Last read it scored US–China tariff CUTS at impact 10.0 and labelled the feed SHOCK. This read it reads CLEAR / 0.0, with a lead story about US House election scenarios.** **On the day a Saudi pipeline is shut, Hormuz diplomacy is postponed, Brent hits a four-month high and QQQ is down 1.45% premarket, the daemon sees nothing.** **It over-scored a de-escalation as a shock and under-scored a physical supply outage as calm. A model that is wrong in both directions is not conservative; it is unanchored.** **I have set `news_shock_score: 6` against the daemon's 0.0, and the observed premarket QQQ move of −1.45% is what calibrates that.**

**Sixth: credit has not been observed across the event that matters, and I am not going to pretend otherwise.** **HY OAS 2.70% and IG OAS 0.80% both carry 2026-09-10 FRED stamps — before the print, before the pipeline closure, before the weekend.** **For twelve reads I described credit as the member holding this report at Stage 3. It may still be. I have no way to know, and the reader should treat the tightest-looking numbers in this report as the oldest ones.**

**Expected move, and a caveat the previous four reads did not need.** With no quoted ATM IV this run, the calculation falls back to the specification's 3×VXN heuristic: **3 × 21.02 = 63.06%**, then **$70.98 × 0.6306 × √(5/252) = $70.98 × 0.6306 × 0.140859 = ±$6.30**, band **$64.68 – $77.28**, or **±8.88%**. **The machine header carries 8.88, the heuristic figure, computed by the same formula as the body.** **But this series has measured the heuristic running 13–15% above the real quote on every one of the six sessions where both existed** (most recently 69.99% heuristic against a 61.0% quote, an overshoot of 14.8%). **Applying that observed bias, the quote-implied expected move would be nearer ±7.7%, or roughly $65.50 – $76.45.
